 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-53-0821 alleging that on 01.06.2020 at 4.30 p.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-HF-2154 from Tavarekere towards Kengeri on Magadi -Tavarekere main road, near Jagadamba Petrol bunk, Kengeri cross, driver of lorry bearing No.KA-53-0821,
drove the same negligently from Tavarekere-Magadi , Bengaluru, from opposite direction , dashed the same to the motorcycle , thereby caused the accident , caused injuries to the petitioner.

3. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged 20 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by working as Electrician .
4.
Regarding accident Tavarekere Traffic police registered crime No.163/2020 .
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 owner of lorry remained absent.

6. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate,
filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner .
7.

On the basis of the pleadings on 03.08.2022 , this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper lorry bearing registration No.KA-53-0821 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was riding the motorcycle bearing reg. No.KA-04-HF-2154 and he sustained injuries in the accident that occurred on 01.06.2020?
2.
Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred on account of negligent act of driver of petitioner himself?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4
. What order?

sentences.text:
In this case on 25.10.2024, on the request of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner produced certificates issued by Dr.Abdul Rawoof which are marked at Ex.P.30 and P.31.
34.

Wound certificate, discharge cards, discharge summaries, clinical notes, prescriptions, case sheets, MRI brain reports, remarks and other medical documents shows that in the accident petitioner has suffered dislocation of right shoulder, undisplace fracture adjacent to right ethimoid sinus with mild pneumo opthalmicus, took treatment at Spine Care and Ortho hospital from 01.06.2022 to 03.06.2022, Sagar hospital from 05.06.2022 to 08.06.2022, HOSMAT hospital from 10.09.2022 to 12.09.2022, by spending approximately Rs.46,500/-.

In the copy of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.17 date of birth of petitioner is noted as 12.05.2000.
35.
In this case , petitioner stated nothing whether he had licence to ride motorcycle or not.
36. In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of the petitioner.
37. In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident .
Hence, I have inferred that the evidence placed by the petitioner are insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income.

38. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place , nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner I award Rs.75,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.46,500/-
towards treatment charges, Rs.20,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.1,01,500/- (14,500x7) towards loss of income during treatment period, Rs.60,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
39. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitled to receive Rs.3,03,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., towards compensation from the respondents.
40. In the written statement , respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to lorry bearing No.KA-53-0821 as on the date of accident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1, owner of the lorry has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of lorry bearing No.KA-53-0821 are liable to pay the compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.3,03,000/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the lorry bearing No.KA-53-0821 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
